papers.title: Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke and ischemic acute kidney injury are both clinical challenges. Danhong injection (DHI) has been reported to exert protective effects against cerebral and renal ischemic injury. However, the shared therapeutic targets and mechanisms underlying its effects in these two organs remain unclear. Using network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro experiments, this study investigated shared targets and pathways associated with cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and evaluated whether DHI exerted a shared ferroptosis-related endot
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and endothelial cell experiments to identify shared therapeutic targets of Danhong injection in both cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury. The authors report that DHI protects endothelial cells through ferroptosis-related mechanisms common to both organs. The work suggests a unifying mechanistic explanation for the injection's cross-organ protective effects.

papers.title: Efficient flavonoids from Helichrysum bracteatum and their multi-target antioxidant mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Helichrysum bracteatum is a promising source of natural antioxidants for food preservation. However, unclear mechanisms and inefficient extraction limit the application of its flavonoids in functional foods. Here, we report a response surface methodology (RSM)-optimized hydroethanolic reflux extraction yielding a maximum flavonoid extraction yield of 16.0% under optimized conditions (27: 1 mL/g, 68% ethanol, 1.6 h). The major flavonoids identified were quercetin (29.44%), kaempferol (8.03%), and rutin (3.44%), and the extract exhibited strong radical-scavenging activity. Network analysis ident
papers.summary: The authors optimized extraction of flavonoids from Helichrysum bracteatum using response surface methodology, achieving a 16.0% yield with quercetin, kaempferol, and rutin as the main components. The extract showed strong radical-scavenging activity, and network analysis was used to explore the multi-target antioxidant mechanisms. This work supports the use of H. bracteatum flavonoids as natural antioxidants for food preservation.

papers.title: Naturallyoccurring phytosterols in lipid nanoparticles induce rigidity reshape and endosome retention to enhance intracellular mRNA processing.
papers.abstract: Although lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have been widely used for mRNA delivery, understanding how cholesterol analogues modulate LNP properties and intracellular trafficking to enhance transfection efficiency remains essential for the rational design of next-generation delivery systems. This study investigated their structure-activity relationships and effects on mRNA delivery. We hypothesized that C-24 alkyl-substituted phytosterols enhance transfection by modulating LNP physicochemical properties and interactions with intracellular transport proteins. These phytosterols altered LNP mechanics an
papers.summary: This study shows that replacing cholesterol in mRNA lipid nanoparticles with naturally occurring phytosterols bearing C-24 alkyl substitutions changes the particles' mechanical rigidity and causes them to be retained longer in endosomes, which paradoxically improves intracellular mRNA processing and transfection efficiency. The work maps structure-activity relationships between sterol chemistry and LNP performance, offering a rational design handle for next-generation mRNA delivery systems.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Hofmeister ion effects on protein properties and their applications in food protein processing: A review.
papers.abstract: The Hofmeister series is a fundamental paradigm for ion-specific regulation of protein properties, with anions playing a dominant role. However, its molecular mechanism remains long-debated, and a systematic synthesis linking basic theory to food protein processing practices is still lacking. This review dissects the action mechanisms of Hofmeister anions from water structure regulation and ion-protein interactions, and summarizes their applications in protein extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization and structural modification. The principal finding is that the Hofmeister effect arises fr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the mechanisms by which Hofmeister series ions—particularly anions—modulate protein properties through water structure regulation and direct ion-protein interactions. It then surveys applications of these effects in food protein processing, including extraction, gelation, emulsion stabilization, and structural modification. The authors argue that the Hofmeister effect arises from a combination of these mechanisms rather than a single dominant cause.

papers.title: Structure-based binding pocket conservation analysis identifies 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylase candidates across phylogenetically diverse bacteria.
papers.abstract: Urolithins are polyphenolic compounds produced by gut microbiota from dietary ellagitannins and ellagic acid, with urolithin A being the most bioactive and associated with a range of pharmaceutical activities like anti-aging and anti-inflammatory effects. Despite these benefits, the number of known urolithin A-producing bacteria and their corresponding enzymes is very limited. In this study, we combined conventional sequence-based homology search with structural modeling to identify novel bacteria potentially harboring 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylases, primarily characterized in the Enterocloster
papers.summary: The authors combined sequence homology searches with structural modeling of binding pockets to identify candidate 9-OH urolithin dehydroxylases in phylogenetically diverse gut bacteria, extending beyond the few known producers such as Enterocloster species. This structure-guided approach expands the limited catalog of bacteria and enzymes capable of converting urolithin precursors into bioactive urolithin A. The work provides new candidate targets for microbiome engineering and functional studies of polyphenol metabolism.

papers.title: CoEVFold suite: User friendly pipelines to visually represent protein coevolution.
papers.abstract: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data underlies current principles in protein folding and protein-protein interaction prediction, from which deep-learning models trained on protein sequence and structure datasets can predict protein structure. However, what is missing are user-friendly tools that enable researchers to identify and visualise coevolution, the principal signal that these MSAs encode. Here we present tools to identify and visualize coevolution, through a pipeline (CoEVFold) that uses basic direct coupling algorithms derived from GREMLIN and an input alignment of sequences from MM
papers.summary: The authors present CoEVFold, a user-friendly software suite that takes a multiple sequence alignment as input and runs direct-coupling analysis (derived from GREMLIN) to identify coevolving residue pairs in proteins. The pipeline then generates visual representations of this coevolutionary signal, which is the key information that underpins modern deep-learning protein structure prediction. The goal is to make coevolution analysis accessible to researchers without requiring custom scripting.

papers.title: Chemical profiling, bioactivity, and machine learning-supported target analysis of Euphorbia macroclada extracts from aerial parts and roots.
papers.abstract: Euphorbia macroclada is used in Anatolian folk medicine, but its chemistry and bioactivity have not been compared across plant parts and extraction solvents. We extracted aerial parts and roots with ethyl acetate, acetone, 70% aqueous acetone and water. The extracts were then profiled by LC-MS/MS and tested in antioxidant and enzyme inhibition assays. UHPLC-ESI-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis showed 101 compounds, mainly flavonoids, hydrolysable tannins, coumarins, and phenolic acid derivatives. The aqueous acetone extracts had the highest phenolic content (up to 86.94 mg GAE per g, roots) and the str
papers.summary: This study compared the chemical composition and bioactivity of Euphorbia macroclada extracts from aerial parts and roots using different solvents. LC-MS/MS identified 101 compounds, mainly flavonoids and tannins, with aqueous acetone extracts showing the highest phenolic content and antioxidant activity. Machine learning was used to support target analysis of the bioactive compounds.

papers.title: AlphaFold models of host-pathogen interactions elucidate the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry.
papers.abstract: Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall
papers.summary: The authors benchmarked AlphaFold2 and AlphaFold3 for predicting structures of host-pathogen protein-protein interactions, finding that accurate models can be retrieved by ranking on modelling confidence despite overall limitations. Using these models, they survey the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry by which pathogen proteins imitate host interfaces to hijack cellular machinery. The work provides a structural lens on how pathogens converge on host interaction interfaces.

papers.title: Large-scale analysis of AlphaFold structures reveals organism-specific physicochemical signatures.
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in protein structure prediction methods have ushered in a new era of abundant and accurate structural data, providing opportunities to analyse proteins at a scale that has not been possible before. Here we performed a large-scale analysis of physicochemical properties across 373,779 confident AlphaFold structures. Our analysis revealed systematic variation between proteins from different organisms to such an extent that major features of the tree of life could be recovered from these data. Surprisingly, this relationship persisted even when we restricted our analysis to euk
papers.summary: The authors analyzed physicochemical properties across 373,779 high-confidence AlphaFold protein structures and found systematic, organism-specific variation that recovers major features of the tree of life. Surprisingly, this phylogenetic signal persisted even when restricting the analysis to eukaryotic proteins, suggesting structural physicochemical signatures carry organism-level information beyond simple taxonomic composition.

papers.title: Effect of amino acid substitutions on the structure and dynamics of human PRPP synthetase PRPS1.
papers.abstract: Phosphoribosylpyrophosphate (PRPP), is required for the synthesis of nucleotides and mutations in human PRPP synthetase (hPRPS1) are linked to Arts syndrome and X-linked Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 5. Here, we investigated mutations linked to these neurological diseases using molecular dynamics simulations. We highlight small but measurable correlations between structural change and kinetic properties as demonstrated by mutant A190V, which exhibits reduced feedback inhibition by ADP and GDP, consistent with superactivity of PRPS1. Changes in RMSD and Rg indicate increased flexibility of mutant Q1
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how disease-linked amino acid substitutions affect the structure and dynamics of human PRPP synthetase (PRPS1), an enzyme required for nucleotide synthesis. The authors find small but measurable correlations between structural changes and kinetic properties, exemplified by mutant A190V showing reduced feedback inhibition by ADP and GDP consistent with enzyme superactivity. Increased flexibility in mutants like Q1 is indicated by changes in RMSD and radius of gyration.

papers.title: Predicting Asymmetric Organocatalysis via Machine-Learning-Driven Molecular Dynamics of Chiral Deep Eutectic Solvents.
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) serve as sustainable, low-volatility, and bio-derived alternatives to conventional organic media, aligning with the demand for green chemical processes. Beyond their role as solvents, they offer transformative potential as integrated catalytic platforms, yet the molecular determinants of their performance remain poorly understood. This study employs machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics combined with density functional theory to investigate the structure and dynamics of chiral deep eutectic solvents in asymmetric catalysis. Simulations reveal that overly pers
papers.summary: This study uses machine-learning-driven molecular dynamics combined with density functional theory to investigate how chiral deep eutectic solvents (DESs) function as catalytic platforms in asymmetric organocatalysis. The simulations reveal that overly persistent hydrogen-bonding networks can hinder catalytic performance, providing molecular-level insight into the structural and dynamic determinants of DES catalytic activity. The work offers a predictive framework for designing greener, bio-derived catalytic solvents.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and molecular dynamics uncover RMJ's targets and mechanisms for treating atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis involves complex pathogenesis including inflammation, lipid disorders, and abnormal autophagy, yet current treatments are limited by adverse reactions and drug resistance, highlighting the need for novel strategies.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify the protein targets and mechanisms through which the traditional formula RMJ may treat atherosclerosis. The approach maps active compounds to atherosclerosis-related targets and validates key interactions computationally, suggesting inflammation, lipid metabolism, and autophagy pathways as likely mechanisms. The work is computational and does not include experimental validation.

papers.title: AARS1-Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post-Transcriptional Reprogramming.
papers.abstract: The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non-histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases (LM) and paired primary tumors (PT) from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), together with multi-omics analyses and in vitro and in vivo validation, identified GLUD1 as a key lactyla
papers.summary: This study integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases versus paired primary tumors in metastatic colorectal cancer patients, identifying GLUD1 as a key lactylated protein. AARS1 mediates lactylation of GLUD1 at lysine 503, which drives metastasis through post-transcriptional reprogramming. The work links the Warburg effect's lactate accumulation to non-histone lactylation as a driver of CRC metastasis.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled natural product pharmacology: From molecular discovery to precision therapeutics.
papers.abstract: The use of natural products as a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules for drug development has been well established; however, their multicomponent and multitarget nature, uncertain target causality, variable in vivo exposure, and heterogeneous responses to therapy make them challenging to characterize pharmacologically and translate into clinical practice. Systems pharmacology, together with artificial intelligence (AI), provides new approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, integration of multidimensional data, and development of precision therapeutics. Osteoarth
papers.summary: This review describes how artificial intelligence combined with systems pharmacology can help overcome the challenges of developing natural products as drugs, including their multi-component and multi-target nature, uncertain target causality, and variable patient responses. The authors outline AI-driven approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, multidimensional data integration, and precision therapeutics, using osteoarthritis as an illustrative case.

papers.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.
papers.summary: This paper expands the clinical phenotype of TUBGCP6-related primary microcephaly, showing that patients can present with severe cortical malformations but without chorioretinopathy, contrary to the classic description. It also provides insights into variant interpretation, noting that most previously reported cases carried at least one loss-of-function variant.

papers.title: Predictive RNA-Ligand Binding Free Energy Perturbation through Preparatory Simulations and Polarizable Force Fields.
papers.abstract: Free energy perturbation (FEP) has become a cornerstone of structure-based drug design, yet its success has been built almost entirely on protein targets. Extending this physical rigor to RNA─an emerging and largely untapped therapeutic target class─confronts challenges that protein-ligand systems rarely impose: pronounced conformational flexibility, dense and highly anisotropic electrostatics, and ligand binding that frequently depends on direct metal coordination. Whether and when these challenges demand more sophisticated physical models has remained an open question. Here, we address it th
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This work extends free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations, a standard tool in protein-based drug design, to RNA-ligand binding by combining preparatory simulations with polarizable force fields. The authors show that RNA's conformational flexibility, anisotropic electrostatics, and metal-coordination-dependent binding require more sophisticated physical modeling than typical protein systems, and identify when such models are needed for accurate predictions.

papers.title: Enhancing Enzyme pH Adaptation for Industrial Biocatalysis: From Sequence-Dependent Engineering to Sequence-Independent Stabilization.
papers.abstract: Enzymes are indispensable biocatalysts in industrial processes, but their application is often restricted by narrow pH optima. Exposure to acidic or alkaline conditions alters the protonation states of ionizable residues, disrupts catalytic microenvironments and stabilizing interactions, and ultimately reduces activity, catalytic efficiency, or structural integrity. This limitation is particularly important in industrial sectors such as detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutic formulations, where operation under non-native pH conditions is frequently required. Conventional sequence
papers.summary: This review examines strategies for improving enzyme performance under non-native pH conditions, which is a major bottleneck for industrial biocatalysis in detergents, textiles, biorefineries, and therapeutics. It distinguishes sequence-dependent engineering approaches (rational design and directed evolution targeting ionizable residues) from sequence-independent stabilization methods, and discusses how acidic or alkaline conditions disrupt protonation states, catalytic microenvironments, and stabilizing interactions.

papers.title: CovPDB 2.0: an expanded covalent protein-ligand interactome.
papers.abstract: The rational design of covalently binding inhibitors to specifically block selected target proteins has become a common strategy in drug discovery. Such design is based on structural insights into how electrophilic ligands bind to nucleophilic residues. CovPDB v1.0 provided high-resolution cocrystal structures of biologically relevant covalent protein-ligand complexes curated from the Protein Data Bank. Here, we describe CovPDB v2.0, a substantially extended release that addresses three main limitations of the original resource. First, to reflect the numerous novel covalently binding ligands d
papers.summary: CovPDB 2.0 is an updated database of high-resolution co-crystal structures showing how covalent ligands bind to protein targets, curated from the Protein Data Bank. The new release substantially expands the number of covalent protein-ligand complexes and addresses key limitations of the original version, supporting structure-based design of covalent inhibitors in drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies have shown that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, identifying it as a promising therap
papers.summary: This study uses AI-based prescreening combined with molecular dynamics simulations to design peptide inhibitors targeting the WWP1 enzyme, which drives PTEN degradation and activates oncogenic PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in breast cancer, particularly triple-negative breast cancer. The work identifies candidate peptide inhibitors as potential therapeutic agents against TNBC, a subtype lacking targeted treatment options.

papers.title: Conformational Plasticity of Orthosteric Pocket Enables the Discovery of a Novel PAD4-Selective Inhibitor.
papers.abstract: Peptidyl-arginine deiminase (PAD) family enzymes are pivotal enzymes that catalyze the citrullination of arginine in substrate proteins. Elevated levels of citrullinated proteins are tightly linked to the incidence of rheumatoid arthritis, neurodegenerative diseases, and cancers, thus highlighting PAD enzymes as important therapeutic targets. Although several PAD isozyme-selective and non-selective small molecule inhibitors have been reported over the last decade, it remains important to identify distinct ligands that may offer differentiated therapeutic potential or selectivity. Herein, we pr
papers.summary: The authors describe the discovery of a novel small-molecule inhibitor that selectively targets PAD4, an enzyme that citrullinates arginine residues and is implicated in rheumatoid arthritis, neurodegeneration, and cancer. The work highlights how conformational flexibility of the enzyme's orthosteric pocket can be exploited to achieve isozyme selectivity, offering a differentiated chemical scaffold for therapeutic development.

papers.title: Nanomaterial-based glucose sensors: detection platforms and highlight applications.
papers.abstract: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved into a severe global public health crisis. Precise, rapid, and stable glucose monitoring is therefore indispensable for the early diagnosis, clinical intervention, and long-term management of diabetes. Conventional enzyme-dependent glucose sensors suffer from inherent limitations, including high manufacturing costs, inferior environmental stability, short serv
papers.summary: This review surveys nanomaterial-based glucose sensing platforms, covering the detection mechanisms and highlighting applications of nanomaterials in improving glucose monitoring. It argues that these platforms can overcome limitations of conventional enzyme-based sensors such as high cost, poor environmental stability, and short shelf life, positioning them as promising tools for diabetes diagnosis and management.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing.
papers.abstract: Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that OH- forms strong chemical bonds with surface Zr atoms, thereby inducing surface hydroxylation and increasing the
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to explain how a NaOH-PVP-water chemical system softens zirconia ceramic surfaces at room temperature, with hydroxide ions bonding to surface zirconium atoms and driving hydroxylation. The work also predicts removal depth during magnetic abrasive finishing, offering a greener alternative to conventional mechanical processing that causes tool wear and microcracks.

papers.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This
papers.summary: This study computationally designs and experimentally tests PSMA-targeted radioconjugates that combine the Glu-urea-Lys binding motif with subcellular-targeting moieties (acridine orange for nuclear delivery, triphenylphosphonium for mitochondrial delivery) to deliver theranostic radiometals to prostate cancer cells. The work explores whether adding subcellular localization signals can enable dual-target approaches beyond conventional PSMA tumor accumulation.

papers.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21-CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach.
papers.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite's secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21-CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host-parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate bin
papers.summary: This study uses consensus-based multi-replica molecular dynamics simulations to model how the Trypanosoma cruzi virulence factor TcP21 binds to the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a key step in Chagas disease host-cell invasion. Since no experimental structure of the complex exists, the authors generate and compare multiple candidate binding poses to identify plausible structural determinants of the interaction. The work provides computational hypotheses for the TcP21-CXCR4 interface that could guide future experimental validation and drug design efforts.

papers.title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF6 Alternative Insulating Gas.
papers.abstract: HFO-1336mzz-(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz-(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. Acute inhal
papers.summary: This study provides the first systematic toxicological evaluation of HFO-1336mzz(E), an environmentally friendly insulating gas proposed as a replacement for SF6, using acute inhalation toxicity testing combined with network toxicology and molecular docking/simulation. The authors identify potential toxicity mechanisms and biological pathways affected by inhalation exposure, supporting the safety assessment of this alternative gas.

papers.title: Investigating Ferritin Permeability to Metal-Based Drugs through Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: In this study, we implemented a workflow based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess whether gold-(I)-containing complexes can traverse the C3 channels of human H ferritin and which energetic barriers were at play in the process. By using two example complexes for which an extensive experimental characterization was already available, we observed that classical MD correctly indicated which one could spontaneously pass through the channel. To quantify the ability of the ferritin nanocage to retain the internalized complex, we estimated, through steered MD and umbrella sampling simula
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to test whether gold-based drug complexes can pass through the C3 channels of human H ferritin, a protein cage that could serve as a drug delivery vehicle. Classical MD correctly predicted which of two experimentally characterized complexes could spontaneously traverse the channel, and steered MD with umbrella sampling quantified the energetic barriers and the cage's ability to retain the internalized complex. The work establishes an MD-based workflow for assessing ferritin permeability to metal-based drugs.

papers.title: Solving the Computational Peptide Design Puzzle: Challenges and Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Peptides are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutics, antimicrobial agents, and supramolecular biomaterials due to the remarkable versatility encoded in their amino acid sequences. However, the rational design of peptides remains challenging because sequence-structure-function relationships are not yet fully understood. Experimental exploration of peptide chemical space is inherently limited by the vast number of possible sequences and the complexity of resolving peptide behavior at molecular resolution. Computational methods, particularly molecular dynamics simulations and, more rec
papers.summary: This review discusses how computational methods, especially molecular dynamics simulations and newer machine-learning approaches, are being used to tackle the rational design of peptides for therapeutics, antimicrobials, and biomaterials. It highlights the core challenge that sequence-structure-function relationships for peptides remain poorly understood and that experimental exploration of peptide sequence space is infeasible, framing computational design as both a puzzle and an opportunity.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto
papers.summary: This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammation. The authors integrate cheminformatics and machine learning approaches to identify and prioritize potential TLR-targeted therapeutics for Mycoplasma infections. It synthesizes immunopathogenesis with computational drug-discovery strategies.

papers.title: Structural Characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ Reveals Membrane-Dependent Stabilization of Its Conserved Electron-Transfer Cofactor Network.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence in granulomas depends on lipid catabolism through the β-oxidation-coupled respiratory pathway, which requires the essential membrane-associated protein IspQ, encoded by Rv0338c. Although IspQ is a genetically and chemically validated drug target, its structural organization and membrane-dependent function remain unknown. Using AlphaFold3 structure prediction, cofactor mapping, evolutionary conservation analysis, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we show that IspQ adopts an EtfD-like fold containing four iron-sulfur clusters, a heme b, and a me
papers.summary: This study uses AlphaFold3 structure prediction and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize IspQ, an essential membrane-associated protein in Mycobacterium tuberculosis required for lipid catabolism during infection. The authors show that IspQ adopts an EtfD-like fold containing four iron-sulfur clusters, a heme b cofactor, and a membrane-binding region, and that its electron-transfer cofactor network is stabilized in a membrane-dependent manner. These structural insights support IspQ as a validated drug target and clarify how it functions at the membrane interface.

papers.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes.
papers.abstract: Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. Simulation results reveal that heteroatom-functionali
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate how windowed carbon nanotube membranes separate CO2 from CH4, examining how nanotube diameter, pressure, feed gas ratio, and nanowindow density affect selectivity. The results indicate that heteroatom functionalization and structural parameters can tune the membrane's molecular sieving performance for gas purification. The work provides theoretical guidance for designing CNT-based membranes for CO2/CH4 separation.

papers.title: Flexible Receptor Docking Provides Structural Models for the Recognition of 2‑Amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide Derivatives by Lck via the CorrEA Method.
papers.abstract: Structural models of Lck bound to a chemically diverse series of 62 2-amino-heteroaryl-benzothiazole-6-anilide (AHBA) inhibitors were built to examine how the conformational state of the ATP-binding site shapes the structure-based interpretation of their potency. Docking to the static Lck crystal structure (PDB entry 1QPC) generated plausible complexes for only 54 of the 62 compounds, and produced essentially no relationship between docking scores and experimental pIC50 values, indicating that a single receptor conformation cannot capture how this scaffold is recognized. Receptor flexibility w
papers.summary: The authors built structural models of the kinase Lck bound to 62 chemically diverse AHBA inhibitors using a flexible-receptor docking method (CorrEA). Docking to a single static crystal structure failed to explain potency for many compounds, whereas allowing receptor flexibility produced models that better capture how this inhibitor scaffold is recognized. The work shows that accounting for ATP-site conformational states is important for structure-based interpretation of inhibitor potency.

papers.title: Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.
papers.abstract: The global dissemination of subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), especially New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase-1 (NDM-1), Verona integron-encoded metallo-β-lactamase-2 (VIM-2), and imipenemase-1 (IMP-1), threatens the clinical utility of carbapenems and other β-lactam antibiotics. This challenge is compounded by the absence of any commercially available MBL inhibitors for clinical use, underscoring the urgent need for novel inhibitor development. Computational approaches now guide much of MBL inhibitor discovery, yet many compounds predicted to bind B1 MBLs, or even shown to inhibit purified en
papers.summary: This review examines why computational methods for discovering subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase inhibitors (targeting NDM-1, VIM-2, IMP-1) have produced many predicted binders that fail to translate into effective inhibitors. It catalogs progress in computational screening and design, identifies common pitfalls such as poor treatment of metal coordination and protein flexibility, and outlines opportunities to improve translational success.

papers.title: Minor Structural Differences Tune Functional Specialization of Antenna Subunits in the PSII Energy Transfer Network.
papers.abstract: Photosystem II (PSII) contains a diverse array of pigment-protein subunits with specialized roles in the antenna network. We investigate the functional significance of this subunit diversity in two structurally similar yet functionally distinct PSII subunits: minor light-harvesting complex CP29 and major light-harvesting complex LHCII. We combine two-dimensional electronic-vibrational spectroscopy with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling to assign spectral features to exciton states, providing molecular detail to probed spectral features. We show how the distinct pig
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.summary: This study investigates how two structurally similar pigment-protein subunits of photosystem II — the minor antenna complex CP29 and the major complex LHCII — achieve distinct functional roles in light harvesting. Using 2D electronic-vibrational spectroscopy combined with lifetime density analysis and structure-based kinetic modeling, the authors assign spectral features to specific exciton states and show that subtle structural differences tune energy transfer behavior. The work provides molecular-level detail linking protein structure to functional specialization within the PSII antenna network.

papers.title: AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.
papers.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum (TPA), an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium (TPANIC), with the goal of providing
papers.summary: The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum Nichols strain. This approach allowed them to assign likely functions to previously uncharacterized proteins and to infer biological and pathogenic properties of the organism from structural similarity rather than sequence alone. The work demonstrates how structure-based annotation can illuminate the biology of a minimal-genome, poorly characterized pathogen.

papers.title: Structure-based discovery of new GPR119 ligands from on-demand tera-scale chemical space.
papers.abstract: The orphan G protein-coupled receptor GPR119 is involved in glucose homeostasis and is considered a promising target for the treatment of diabetes and other metabolic diseases. The recently solved structures of GPR119 in complex with potential endogenous lipid agonists, including oleoylethanolamide (OEA), provide a solid platform for 3D pharmacology analysis and structure-based ligand discovery. Here, we employed the V-SYNTHES2 approach to screen ∼3 trillion on-demand compounds from Enamine xREAL chemical space to identify several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. Structure-gu
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors used the V-SYNTHES2 structure-based virtual screening method to search a ~3 trillion compound on-demand chemical space (Enamine xREAL) against recently solved GPR119 structures, identifying several new chemotypes of GPR119 agonists and antagonists. This demonstrates that tera-scale on-demand libraries can yield novel ligands for a metabolically relevant GPCR target.

papers.title: A Hybrid Ligand- and Structure-Based Drug Design Invoked through Square Attention in Protein-Ligand Transformer.
papers.abstract: Computer-aided molecular design based on evaluation of protein-ligand (PL) binding affinity is important for accelerating drug discovery. A deep-learning model for natural language processing (NLP) involving an attention mechanism (i.e., Transformer) is expected to improve the PL-affinity evaluation along with clarifying amino acid residues and ligand atoms that are responsible for molecular interactions. However, the original attention (i.e., a scaled dot-product with row-wise Softmax normalization) is an adapted method for relationships between homogeneous inputs (e.g., two sentences in the
papers.summary: The authors introduce a 'square attention' mechanism for a protein-ligand Transformer that better captures interactions between heterogeneous inputs (protein residues and ligand atoms), enabling simultaneous ligand- and structure-based drug design. The model evaluates binding affinity while identifying the specific amino acid residues and ligand atoms responsible for interactions, supporting interpretable molecular design.

papers.title: CB-Smart: A Cloud-Based Machine Learning Platform for Screening Cannabinoid Receptor Ligands.
papers.abstract: Cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2 are class A G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) implicated in pain modulation, neuroinflammation, immune regulation, and metabolic processes, making them important therapeutic targets. Conventional structure-based virtual screening for cannabinoid ligands remains computationally intensive and limited in throughput. To overcome this challenge, this work presents CB-Smart, a cloud-enabled machine learning (ML) platform to predict binding of ligands and their relative binding affinity to CB1 and CB2. Using curated experimentally validated ligands and GPCR decoy d
papers.summary: CB-Smart is a cloud-based machine learning platform that predicts whether a ligand binds to cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2 and estimates its relative binding affinity. It was trained on curated experimentally validated ligands and GPCR decoys, offering a faster alternative to conventional structure-based virtual screening. The tool aims to speed up early-stage drug discovery for pain, neuroinflammation, and metabolic targets.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a systematic benchmark for predicting protein-ligand binding sites at the residue level, evaluating models across three data-availability regimes: ligands with abundant training examples, underrepresented ligands, and zero-shot ligands never seen during training. The framework uses a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering and a progressive three-stage evaluation, highlighting how predictive performance varies by ligand family and data availability.

papers.title: Structure-Based Discovery of GTP-Enhanced Rab10 Modulators and Their Effects on Alzheimer's Disease-Relevant Cellular Phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Rab10-mediated membrane trafficking has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but pharmacological tools for investigating its function remain limited. Here, we screened more than 80 million compounds using structure-based virtual screening and prioritized five candidate Rab10 modulators ( R1-R5 ). These compounds exhibited favorable docking scores, stable modeled protein-ligand complexes in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and predicted acceptable ADME/toxicity profiles. Comparative docking against Rab5, Rab8, and Rab11 predicted preferential interactions with GTP-associated Rab10. R
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Researchers used structure-based virtual screening of over 80 million compounds to identify five candidate modulators of the Rab10 GTPase, a protein involved in membrane trafficking and implicated in Alzheimer's disease. The compounds showed favorable docking, stable complexes in molecular dynamics simulations, and acceptable predicted drug-like properties, with preferential binding to the GTP-bound form of Rab10 over related Rab proteins. This provides initial pharmacological tools for probing Rab10 function in AD-relevant cellular contexts.

papers.title: Large-Scale Prospective Virtual Screening Using a Co-Folding-Rescoring Workflow for NPM1-TYK2 Inhibitor Discovery.
papers.abstract: Conventional large-scale structure-based virtual screening typically relies on fixed-receptor docking, in which ligand poses are sampled against a predefined receptor conformation. Protein-ligand co-folding models can instead generate candidate complex conformations by jointly modeling ligand placement and local receptor-ligand structural adaptation. Although recent benchmark studies have demonstrated the promise of AlphaFold3-like approaches for retrospective virtual screening, their practical application to target-specific, large-scale prospective screening with experimental validation remai
papers.summary: This study demonstrates a large-scale prospective virtual screening workflow that uses protein-ligand co-folding models (AlphaFold3-like) to generate candidate complex conformations, followed by rescoring, to discover inhibitors targeting the NPM1-TYK2 interaction. Unlike conventional fixed-receptor docking, the approach allows local receptor-ligand structural adaptation, and the authors validate hits experimentally. It provides a practical, target-specific example of applying co-folding to prospective screening rather than retrospective benchmarking.

papers.title: Synthesis and Evaluation of Novel Derivatives of 3,4,5-Trisubstituted Triazole as Potential Cyclooxygenase Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: The series of [2-[(5-(4-aminophenyl)-4-phenyl-4H-1,2,4-triazol-3-yl)thio]-N-(thiazol-2-yl)]acetamide derivatives (C1-C12) were designed, synthesized, evaluated in vitro against the cyclooxygenase enzymes COX-1 and COX-2, and characterized by HRMS, 1H-NMR, and 13C-NMR spectroscopy. The series displayed a diverse inhibition profile: C7 and C9 emerged as potent dual COX-1/COX-2 inhibitors, with C7 being the most active COX-2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.308 ± 0.014 μM), whereas C3 and C6 acted as highly COX-1-selective inhibitors (IC50 = 0.083 and 0.096 μM, respectively), and C10 showed a COX-2-selective
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of twelve novel triazole-based acetamide derivatives and tested them in vitro against the COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes. Several compounds showed potent inhibition, with C7 being the strongest COX-2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.308 μM), while C3 and C6 were highly COX-1-selective, and C10 was COX-2-selective. This provides new chemical scaffolds for developing selective or dual COX inhibitors.

papers.title: Immunoinformatic and Structural Design of an Influenza A DNA Vaccine Based on Conserved Nucleoprotein Epitopes and Heat Shock Protein 70 Adjuvant.
papers.abstract: Influenza A is a health concern, as it constantly mutates and changes antigens. The conventional vaccine is not very effective in providing immunity. We have designed and characterized a DNA multi-epitope vaccine based on conserved regions of the influenza A nucleoprotein (NP) and have assessed the immune response.
papers.summary: This study uses immunoinformatics and structural modeling to design a DNA vaccine against influenza A, built from conserved nucleoprotein epitopes and an HSP70 adjuvant. The authors computationally predict and characterize the construct's ability to elicit immune responses, aiming to overcome the limitations of conventional vaccines that struggle with viral antigenic drift. The work is a computational design study, with experimental validation not described in the abstract.

papers.title: Diversity at the Acinetobacter baumannii K locus: towards a comprehensive database for in silico prediction of capsular polysaccharide types.
papers.abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is one of the most critical bacterial pathogens requiring novel approaches for infection control and treatment to curb the spread of highly resistant isolates. Epidemiological surveillance and the design and application of many non-antibiotic interventions require rapid and accurate prediction of diverse capsular polysaccharide (CPS) types from whole-genome sequence data. The internationally adopted CPS typing system relies on the in silico detection of CPS biosynthesis genes both in and outside the K locus (KL), utilizing a reference sequence database that is compatibl
papers.summary: This paper expands the reference database used to predict capsular polysaccharide (CPS) types in Acinetobacter baumannii from whole-genome sequence data. By cataloguing additional diversity at the K locus, it improves the accuracy and coverage of in silico CPS typing, which is important for surveillance and for designing non-antibiotic interventions against this highly resistant pathogen.

papers.title: Computer-Aided Drug Design for Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming: A Critical Review.
papers.abstract: How can cellular interactions in solid tumors guide molecular interventions against immune suppression? This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) connects immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) states to testable molecular hypotheses. We distinguish observational artificial intelligence (AI) predictions from molecular intervention hypotheses and examine the experimental evidence required to evaluate them. We reviewed patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, molecular design, simulation, and pharmacology using literature identified through 15
papers.summary: This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) can be used to reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in solid tumors. It distinguishes observational AI predictions from actionable molecular intervention hypotheses and outlines the experimental evidence needed to validate them, drawing on patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, molecular design, simulation, and pharmacology.

papers.title: Structural Determinants of Biologic Recognition Across GPCR Classes.
papers.abstract: The rapid increase in experimentally resolved G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-biologic complexes has substantially improved our understanding of the molecular basis of receptor recognition and modulation. However, despite the growing number of available structures, a comparative framework integrating the major GPCR classes is still lacking. In this review, we analysed experimentally resolved GPCR-biologic complexes across receptor Classes A, B, C, and F to identify the structural principles governing biologic recognition. Our analysis shows that the architecture of each GPCR class shapes dis
papers.summary: This review compares experimentally resolved structures of GPCR–biologic complexes across receptor Classes A, B, C, and F to identify shared and class-specific structural principles of biologic recognition. The authors show that each GPCR class's architecture shapes how biologics (e.g., antibodies, nanobodies, peptides) engage the receptor, providing a comparative framework that was previously lacking.

papers.title: Aggregate-associated interfacial organization of sodium oleate near zircon surfaces.
papers.abstract: Sodium oleate (NaOL) is widely used as an anionic collector for zircon flotation, yet its heterogeneous organization at zircon surfaces remains insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the anionic collector sodium oleate organizes at zircon surfaces, a key process in zircon flotation. Using interfacial characterization, the authors show that NaOL forms aggregate-associated structures at the zircon-water interface rather than a uniform monolayer. The work provides a more detailed picture of collector adsorption that could inform flotation efficiency.

papers.title: Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics-Based Investigation of the Potential Anti-Inflammatory and Cell-Survival Regulatory Mechanisms of Dapansutrile in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterised by persistent synovial inflammation, progressive cartilage and bone destruction, and disability. Existing therapies can be limited by adverse effects and cost, and additional treatment approaches remain of interest. Dapansutrile (OLT1177) is an orally active, selective inhibitor of the NLRP3 inflammasome that has shown anti-inflammatory activity and good tolerability in early clinical studies. Whether dapansutrile might also interact with other RA-related proteins has not been examined specifically in RA. This study used c
papers.journal: Open access rheumatology : research and reviews
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to explore how dapansutrile, an NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor, might interact with proteins relevant to rheumatoid arthritis beyond its known target. The work suggests potential anti-inflammatory and cell-survival regulatory mechanisms, but the findings are computational predictions that would require experimental validation.

papers.title: Correction: Integrated AUF-UPLC-MS and fraction-activity correlation to identify COX-2-targeted constituents of Shaoyao Gancao decoction.
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.3389/fchem.2026.1912431.].
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article that used AUF-UPLC-MS and fraction-activity correlation to identify COX-2-targeted constituents of Shaoyao Gancao decoction. The correction itself does not report new findings; it only amends the original publication.

papers.title: AI-driven strategies for Cas12 protein design and genome editing optimization.
papers.abstract: The rise of the CRISPR-CAS system has greatly promoted the development of gene editing technology. Cas12, with its unique molecular characteristics, has become an important editing tool following Cas9. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in Cas12-related research, ranging from protein structure optimization, target design to editing efficiency prediction and off-target risk assessment. AI has demonstrated great potential in enhancing system performance and discovering new mutants. Most of these models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines, E. coli,
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is being applied to improve Cas12-based CRISPR genome editing, covering protein structure optimization, guide RNA design, editing efficiency prediction, and off-target risk assessment. It highlights AI's potential to enhance Cas12 system performance and discover new protein variants, while noting that most models were trained and benchmarked in human cell lines and E. coli.

papers.title: Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and modulates wnt/ β  -catenin signaling and androgen receptor conformational dynamics.
papers.abstract: Dermal papilla cells regulate hair follicle growth, yet bioactive peptides that influence both pro-growth signaling and androgen receptor (AR)-associated regulation remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effects of Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) on human dermal papilla cell function and its potential interaction with the AR ligand-binding domain (AR-LBD).
papers.summary: This study shows that Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) stimulates proliferation of human dermal papilla cells, the cells that control hair follicle growth, and appears to modulate Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Computational analysis also suggests MT12 can interact with the androgen receptor ligand-binding domain, hinting at a role in androgen-related hair regulation. The work is early-stage and largely in vitro/in silico, so clinical relevance for hair loss remains to be established.

papers.title: PARP1 and PD-L1 dual-targeted bifunctional small-molecule inhibitors: a novel strategy for dual immunotherapy of triple-negative breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Current single-agent PD-L1 immunotherapy and PARP inhibitor combination regimens have several drawbacks, including limited response rates, mismatched pharmacokinetics, and overlapping toxicities. This research aims to discover novel bifunctional small molecules that simultaneously block the PD-1/PD-L1 axis and PARP1, with prominent selectivity for PARP subtypes, to overcome bottlenecks in triple-negative breast cancer immunotherapy.
papers.summary: This paper describes the discovery of bifunctional small molecules that simultaneously inhibit PARP1 and PD-L1, aiming to overcome the limitations of combining separate PARP inhibitors and PD-L1 immunotherapies in triple-negative breast cancer. The approach seeks to improve response rates and reduce pharmacokinetic mismatches and overlapping toxicities by targeting both pathways with a single agent.

papers.title: Multitarget docking and toxicity-guided prioritisation of phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against wheat fungal pathogens.
papers.abstract: The rising issue of fungicide resistance, along with environmental concerns related to synthetic fungicides, highlights the need for safer and more sustainable antifungal agents. In this computational study, we screened nineteen phytochemicals from locally available medicinal plants in Bangladesh against three fungal protein targets associated with major wheat diseases: class I sesquiterpene synthase (PDB ID: 8H4P) and trichothecene 3-O-acetyltransferase (TRI101; PDB ID: 3B2S) from Fusarium graminearum, and the AvrSr50 effector protein (PDB ID: 7MQQ) from Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici. Blin
papers.summary: This computational study screened nineteen phytochemicals from Bangladeshi medicinal plants against three fungal protein targets linked to major wheat diseases (Fusarium graminearum and Puccinia graminis). Using multitarget molecular docking combined with toxicity-guided prioritisation, the authors identified candidate phytochemicals with favourable binding and safety profiles as potential sustainable antifungal agents. The work is purely in silico and requires experimental validation.

papers.title: An OGE-HPLC-ABTS-Q-TOF MS Screening of Antioxidant Components in Gushuning Tablet (GSN) With Computational Prediction of Related Biological Targets.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a severe skeletal disorder that poses a major threat to public health, and oxidative stress may be one of its core pathological mechanisms. The Traditional Chinese Medicine compound preparation Gushuning Tablet (GSN) has been reported to show potential clinical benefits in OP, potentially related to the modulation of OP-associated oxidative stress. However, its antioxidant active material basis and mechanism of action remain unclear. This study aimed to establish an online gradient extraction (OGE)-high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-2,2'-azinobis-(3-ethylbenzthi
papers.summary: This study combines online gradient extraction HPLC with an ABTS antioxidant assay and Q-TOF mass spectrometry to screen and identify antioxidant compounds in the traditional Chinese medicine Gushuning Tablet, a preparation used for osteoporosis. The identified compounds were then analyzed with computational target prediction to propose biological targets linking them to oxidative stress pathways relevant to osteoporosis. The work provides a chemical basis for the tablet's purported antioxidant activity but relies on in silico predictions rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders. However, the systems-level connections among PFAS-associated molecular perturbations, immune dysregulation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to prioritize candidate links between PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation to identify molecular links between PFAS exposure and immune-inflammatory dysregulation in COPD. The authors prioritize candidate PFAS-associated targets that overlap with COPD transcriptional and inflammatory signatures, highlighting potential mechanistic connections between environmental contaminant exposure and respiratory disease.

papers.title: Identification of novel compounds from Olea Europaea targeting hDus2 as potential anticancer agents: a molecular docking and molecular dynamics study.
papers.abstract: Leukemia, a type of blood cancer, ranks among the top causes of cancer-related fatalities. Human tRNA-dihydrouridine synthase 2 (hDus2) catalyzes the conversion of uridine to dihydrouridine in the tRNA and is overexpressed in cancer cells, facilitating the translational process required for cancer cell growth. Inhibition of hDus2 reduces cancer cell growth and viability while increasing apoptosis sensitivity under stress, making it an excellent cancer target. Olea Europaea is known to be abundant in flavonoids, polyphenols, vitamins, and antioxidants, and shows immense potential in providing h
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen compounds from Olea Europaea (olive) for binding to hDus2, a tRNA-modifying enzyme overexpressed in leukemia cells that supports cancer growth. The authors identify candidate natural compounds that may inhibit hDus2, proposing them as potential anticancer agents. The work is entirely computational, with no experimental validation of binding or anticancer activity.

papers.title: SLC38A2-Driven Glutamine Metabolic Reprogramming Promotes Hypoxic Survival in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is highly refractory to standard therapies, including anti-angiogenic agents such as bevacizumab. While bevacizumab prunes tumor vasculature, it exacerbates intratumoral hypoxia, which drives a metabolically resilient phenotype that limits survival benefits. This study aimed to identify the metabolic dependencies underlying GBM adaptation to hypoxia and to evaluate whether targeting these dependencies could enhance the antitumor efficacy of bevacizumab. Methods: We analyzed the spatial distribution of key metabolites in GBM patients and orthotopic xenograft mouse
papers.summary: This study identifies SLC38A2, a glutamine transporter, as a key driver of metabolic reprogramming that allows glioblastoma cells to survive under hypoxia. Targeting this glutamine dependency may improve the antitumor efficacy of the anti-angiogenic drug bevacizumab, which otherwise worsens intratumoral hypoxia.

papers.title: Advances in injectable liposome-microspheres platforms for osteoarthritis therapy: from sustained delivery to multifunctional disease modification.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, whole-joint disorder marked by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodeling, synovial inflammation, and capsular fibrosis, affecting over 500 million individuals worldwide. Current pharmacotherapies are mainly palliative, with no approved disease-modifying osteoarthritis drugs (DMOADs). Intra-articular (IA) injection provides direct joint access but is hampered by rapid drug clearance and short residence times. Injectable liposome-microsphere (iLMP) systems have recently emerged as integrative delivery platforms that synergistically combine t
papers.summary: This review examines injectable liposome-microsphere (iLMP) platforms for treating osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disease affecting over 500 million people with no approved disease-modifying drugs. These systems combine liposomes and microspheres to extend drug retention in the joint after intra-articular injection and to enable multifunctional disease modification beyond simple symptom relief. The authors survey recent advances and argue that iLMP platforms could bridge the gap between palliative care and true disease-modifying therapy.

papers.title: Structure-based computational screening of cyclotides as putative CYP19A1-binding scaffolds for modulation of estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis.
papers.abstract: Adenomyosis is a chronic estrogen-dependent gynecological disorder associated with dysmenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and recurrent implantation failure. Because human placental aromatase cytochrome P450 (CYP19A1) plays a central role in local estrogen biosynthesis, this study employed an integrated in silico workflow to identify cyclotide scaffolds capable of interacting with CYP19A1. The receptor structure was prepared and validated, while protein-protein interaction analysis confirmed its involvement in steroidogenesis and estrogen biosynthesis. Twent
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and molecular dynamics to screen cyclotide peptides for binding to CYP19A1 (aromatase), the enzyme that produces estrogen, aiming to find scaffolds that could modulate estrogen biosynthesis in adenomyosis. The work is entirely in silico, identifying putative cyclotide binders as starting points for future experimental validation rather than demonstrating activity.

papers.title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies.
papers.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. However, the concurrent challenges of implant-associated bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration remain formidable obstacles in clinical practice. Rather than being independent processes, bacterial infection and bone regeneration are intimately coupled through a complex signaling network-a concept increasingly recognized a
papers.summary: This review examines how titanium dioxide nanotube (TNT) surfaces, made by anodization, can be engineered to address both bacterial infection and poor bone integration around orthopedic and dental implants. It argues that infection and bone formation are not separate problems but are linked through shared signaling pathways, and it surveys design strategies that exploit this crosstalk to create implants with combined antibacterial and osteogenic properties.
